rationale: The Shootout 'random' benchmark is a tiny, compute-bound program whose hot path is a tight integer-arithmetic loop (an LCG-style generator), so the priority is cheap data-level obfuscation with strict cost penalties on control-flow transforms. SUB gets the highest security and diversity weights because arithmetic substitution directly obscures the generator's magic constants and is essentially free in both time and space with minimal correctness risk. SPLIT is similarly cheap and safe and earns a moderate diversity weight to fragment the few functions without measurable overhead. FLA and BCF receive high RuntimeCost (0.8/0.9) and SizeCost (0.6/0.8) weights so the selector applies them only to cold functions, if at all — flattening or bogus-control-flowing the hot loop would dominate the benchmark's runtime. IBR and ICALL get mid-range security/diversity weights tempered by moderate runtime and correctness penalties: this program has few functions and call sites, so indirect branching/calling adds limited reverse-engineering value relative to its dispatch overhead and its higher chance of miscompiling indirect targets. IGV's global indirection would penalize the loop's frequent global state accesses, so its RuntimeCost weight (0.7) keeps it mostly off except where globals are rarely touched.
